I am an external auditor, and during an audit I read about two hundred emails from the client. I can tell you which ones I answer first. They tell me in the first line why they are writing. Regarding your question about the March adjustment. Then one sentence with the answer, and the file is attached. If something is still pending, they say so, and they give me a date. The emails I leave for later are the long ones, with three paragraphs of thank you and hope you are well before I find the information. And the ones that worry me are the vague ones. If there is a problem, I would much rather read: it appears that the entry was posted twice, we are checking it, and we will confirm by Thursday. That sentence does not scare me. It tells me the client found it first.

For two years, I wrote every email in Spanish and asked the AI to translate it. It worked, and the emails were perfect. Then one day the director called me, right after I sent an update, and asked me two questions about it. I could not answer in English. I did not know the words, because I had never really written them. So I changed one thing. Now I write the draft myself, in English, even if it is slow and not perfect. I read it out loud once. Then I ask the AI to check it, and I look at every change it makes. My emails take ten minutes longer. But when the director calls, the words are already in my mouth.
